definition: Training on many GPUs that each hold a full copy of the model and process a different slice of the batch, then average their gradients with an all-reduce every step.
Splitting each layer's weight matrices across several GPUs so they compute one layer together; it needs an all-reduce inside every layer, so it is kept within a fast NVLink domain.
Cutting a model's layers into consecutive stages on different GPUs and streaming micro-batches through them like an assembly line; only activations cross stage boundaries.
The idle time in pipeline parallelism while stages wait for the line to fill and drain; for p stages and m micro-batches it is about (p − 1)/(m + p − 1) of each step.
A small slice of a training batch processed as one unit through a pipeline; more micro-batches per step shrink the pipeline bubble.
Placing the different experts of a mixture-of-experts model on different GPUs, so tokens must be sent to their chosen experts and back with all-to-all exchanges every MoE layer.
The small learned network in a mixture-of-experts layer that scores the experts for each token and picks which few will process it.
Splitting the tokens of one very long sequence across GPUs, which then exchange attention keys and values (for example around a ring); used for 100K-token-plus training.
NVIDIA's companion to tensor parallelism that splits operations such as LayerNorm along the sequence dimension to save activation memory at no extra communication; distinct from context parallelism.
Microsoft's technique for sharding optimizer states (stage 1), gradients (stage 2) and weights (stage 3) across data-parallel GPUs instead of replicating them, cutting memory per GPU.
PyTorch's built-in implementation of fully sharded data parallelism (ZeRO stage 3 style): weights are all-gathered just before use and gradients reduce-scattered after.
A communication pattern in which a whole group of GPUs exchanges data at once (all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter, all-to-all, broadcast), as opposed to one GPU sending to another.
A collective in which each GPU contributes a slice and every GPU ends up with all the slices concatenated.
A collective in which GPUs sum their vectors but each GPU keeps only its own slice of the result; the first half of a ring all-reduce.
A collective in which every GPU sends a different piece of data to every other GPU at once; the communication pattern of mixture-of-experts layers and the hardest for a network.
An all-reduce algorithm that passes chunks around a ring of GPUs; each GPU sends about twice the data size regardless of how many GPUs take part.
